newsitem.title: MEXICO: Jailed Mexico priests say they were tortured.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Mexico priests say they were tortured.

text.p: Two Mexican priests and two Indian peasants jailed in the southern state of Chiapas on murder charges alleged on Wednesday they had been tortured and said evidence against them was rigged.

One of the Jesuit priests, Gonzalo Rosas, told CBS Telenoticias television who interviewed him in jail that he had been held down and struck with a pistol while in custody. His fellow detainees showed reporters burns and bruises.
"They put me face down and were giving it to me. Then they gave me a blow with a pistol butt -- I still have the reminder here," he said, rubbing a lump on the back of his neck.

Rosas and fellow priest Geronimo Hernandez were seized along with the two Indian activists on Saturday, accused of killing two policemen and injuring five others in an ambush after police evicted a group of peasants from occupied land.
Their case has been taken up by the normally conservative Roman Catholic Church in Mexico City as well as human rights groups, who said the priests were elsewhere when the policemen were slain.
The peasants say the killings occurred when police, backed by a helicopter, started shooting at them and they fired back.

"I don't know exactly why I'm here. The authorities, when an Indian raises his voice, closes his mouth with this type of punishment," said Francisco Gonzalez, one of the Indians, showing burns high up his thigh.
He said the arrests were probably aimed at tarnishing the work of the priests on behalf of peasants in the turbulent state, where an armed Indian uprising has festered since 1994.

Hernandez is also charged with carrying arms, though he told CBS Telenoticias that a gun was planted on him after his arrest. "They plant bodies, pistols -- each day there is more evidence of corruption," the priest said.

In Mexico City, the Interior Ministry's undersecretary for religious affairs, Rafael Rodriguez, denied the four men were being held on political grounds. He told reporters he had told high officials in the Catholic Church they could defend the priests in a court of law.
The official did not comment on allegations of torture.
